build.summary:
I built access-closure-femoral-manual: the femoral closure algorithm with its angiogram presets, then hands-on manual compression in the full case.

New pure modules:
- src/simulation/access/closurePlan.ts holds the four questions in order and the rules: no device below the bifurcation, in a branch, under 5 mm or in diseased artery; no collagen plug in a high stick; no suture device in heavy calcium; no hand compression at an ACT of 180 s or more; the sheath kept for a staged PCI or support device, with a long sheath swapped for 10-13 cm; a device above an ACT of 300 s is scored acceptable with a caution. Answers and choices are graded.
- src/simulation/access/compression.ts holds the Brilakis or Oxford rule for the ACT and the timer (2-3 min per Fr, or 8-10 min), the preparation checklist, protamine dosing (1-1.5 mg per 100 U, capped at 50 mg, refused while equipment is in, a reaction 5-10 min later that is more likely with a fast injection) and a finger model: coverage of the hole, the pressure needed to hold it, oozing, a groin swelling, the plug forming and occlusive pressure cutting distal flow. Each value is quoted from 13-closure.ts or labelled MODEL PARAMETER.

In caseSession.ts:
- New public methods: setClosureContext, relocateTeamPuncture (for scenario start states only), closureEndState, closureAnatomy, answerClosureQuestions, chooseClosure, reprepSkin, setCompressionRule, confirmPrep (sends saline and the vagal kit through the emergencies module), lowerBloodPressure, giveProtamine, startCompression, setHands, holdCompression, compressionFeel, compressionTimer, releaseCompression, checkGroin, checkFootPulses and applyDressing.
- Lifting the hands before the plug holds makes the puncture bleed again.
- The release feeds femoralRisk with the time-weighted position error, the pressure adequacy and the systolic pressure at the pull. femoralRisk gained these as optional terms, so earlier callers get the same results.
- A sheath kept for a staged PCI closes the site with the sheath in.
- 'act-high' is added to CASE_SESSION_EVENTS. It is held from an ACT measured at 180 s or more at a femoral closure until a lower reading or the pull. Blood at the skin nick raises 'bleeding', and a visible swelling holds 'haematoma'.
- Pulling a venous sheath before the arterial one in the same groin is scored.
- femoralDevice takes an optional device kind; femoralManual is unchanged, so the autopilot is unaffected.

There are 11 scenarios in scenarios/closureFemoral.ts, with a matching .launch.ts, all starting at 'closure'. The vagal and tamponade look-alikes reuse the emergencies module's scripts and treatments.

UI:
- GroinView.tsx: draggable fingers, the crease, the felt pulse, the skin nick, blood at the nick and a visible swelling. The arterial hole is drawn only as a guided aid.
- ClosurePanel.tsx: the femoral artery block now has the ACT, the angiogram plus a link to read it on fluoroscopy, the four questions (their answers shown only in guided mode), the closure choices, and the compression controls (pressure slider, hold 1 or 2 min, release, timer, the operator's feel line) followed by the aftercare checks.
- orders/Compression.tsx: the checklist, the rule, BP lowering and protamine with a slow or push rate.

acceptance.criterion: closurePlan rejects a collagen plug for 'closure-fem-high-stick' and any device for 'closure-fem-below-bif' and 'closure-fem-small-artery'
acceptance.evidence: closurePlan.test.ts uses the scenarios' real anatomy. High stick: highStick is true, collagen-plug is graded wrong with a 'high stick' reason, and suture-device is correct at the scenario's ACT, which is at or below 300 s. Below-bif (atOrBelowBifurcation) and small artery (over5mm false, 4.5 mm CFA): both devices are graded wrong. In the session, chooseClosure('suture-device') below the bifurcation records femoral-closure-choice as incorrect.

acceptance.criterion: Hand compression at ACT 240 s is wrong and after waiting to 170 s correct; protamine before the catheter is out is refused; 80 mg is capped or scored wrong
acceptance.evidence: compression.test.ts: compression-act-high opens with a measured ACT of 225-255 s and 'act-high' is active. chooseClosure('manual-compression') is graded wrong there, and correct after waiting and measuring until the ACT is at or below 170. startCompression then records femoral-act as correct; pulling at the opening ACT records it as wrong. giveProtamine with the catheter in (start 'post-diagnostic') is refused, nothing is given and the dose decision is wrong. 80 mg gives 50 mg, scored wrong, and the ACT falls.

acceptance.criterion: Compression 15 mm caudal to the arteriotomy raises the large-haematoma risk over the centred value
acceptance.evidence: compression.test.ts, pure: femoralRisk with the position error of fingers 15 mm caudal of the hole gives a higher largeHaematoma than centred (and with 15 mm passed directly). In the session, pressing 15 mm below the hole for 4 min, then moving over it, gives a larger femoral.positionErrorMm and largeHaematoma than a centred compression, raises bleeding and haematoma, and the groin check shows a swelling.

acceptance.criterion: 'compression-vagal' gives HR below 50 before MAP below 65, restored by atropine and fluid with pressure kept; 'compression-tamponade-mimic' gives HR above 100 with hypotension and an effusion on echo
acceptance.evidence: compression.test.ts: in compression-vagal, after startCompression the HR goes below 50 before the MAP goes below 65 and bradycardia is raised. With legs up, atropine 0.5 mg and fluid 500 mL given through the emergencies module while the compression stays on (not released, pressure above 0.5), the HR is at least 50, the MAP at least 65 and the nick is dry. An untreated control at the same time is still below. compression-tamponade-mimic (with preparation done) reaches HR above 100 with MAP below 65, raises hypotension, and the echo order returns a pericardial effusion.

build.notes:
Snapshots of the three files that already existed (closure.ts, caseSession.ts, ClosurePanel.tsx) are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/access-closure-femoral-manual/ with a .started marker. Only listed files plus one new test file were edited. To confirm the scenarios.test.ts failure was already there, I briefly swapped the snapshot caseSession.ts in for one test run and then restored my version.

Design decisions:
- Closure scenarios can't set where the autopilot punctures. For the high stick, below-bifurcation and branch presets, a public session method, relocateTeamPuncture, moves the team's arteriotomy, its needle track and the plugged hole together. It is meant only for scenario start states.
- The tamponade look-alike's pericardial cap is 140 mL, so this 69-year-old still has a fast rate and a low pressure with saline running. The emergency scenarios use 155 mL.
- compression-act-high tops up heparin to the PCI dose, then lets the team's time pass (engine ACT, nothing recorded as measured) until the ACT is about 245 s.
- At the pull the session writes a provisional femoral record (0 minutes), so the emergencies module's removal-drill scoring still sees a manual compression. The site is not closed until the release.
- The BP-lowering order names no drug or dose because the lesson names none; its effect is a model parameter.

Behaviour notes:
- In the UI the fingers start on the skin nick, so the learner has to drag them above it.
- The four questions and the closure choice are recorded but only graded on screen in guided mode. The arterial hole is drawn only in guided mode (policy.overlays.labels).
- In the tips test the vagal reaction is scripted by the test at level 1, because closure-fem-standard's patient only reaches about 50 bpm at the default level.

review.verdict: Approve once two major fixes are made. The design is almost fully built. tsc is clean. The package's 3 test files pass (28/28), and so do caseSession, multiSite, emergencies, caseTips.reach and reachability (67/67). Every sourced number I checked matches 13-closure.ts: 180 s, 300 s, 5 mm, 10-13 cm, 2-3 min per Fr, Oxford 8-10 min and 150-200 s or 3-4 h, protamine 1-1.5 mg per 100 U to 50 mg with a reaction 5-10 min later, 90 days, and 1 cm proximal. Shared engines keep their defaults: femoralRisk's new terms are optional, and femoralManual and the autopilot are unchanged. The other src files changed since .started belong to the pacing, bench-measure and pressure packages. I checked the browser criterion in my own tab on the dev server: in closure-fem-standard, dragging the GroinView fingers above the hole gave 'fingers on average 0 mm from it, correct'. Leaving them on the nick for 4 min, then dragging them up, gave 3.7 mm, blood at the nick and 'haematoma'. So dragging does change the debrief. Two problems block approval: the UI has no way to wait for the ACT to fall, and the true ACT is shown live without being measured. The rest are minor.

findings.problem: The case UI has no control to make time pass (ProcedureLab's clock runs in real time, and 'Skip ahead' only finishes time already pending). Choosing 'Suture the sheath in, wait for the ACT to fall, then compress' only spends sheathS and writes a log line. In the browser, compression-act-high (opens at about 245 s) and any femoral case with an ACT of 180 s or more cannot reach the plan's 'ACT falls with heparin decay during a wait' except through protamine. The tests get round this with session.wait(), which no UI calls.
findings.fix: In FemoralClosure, while the sheath is in and there is no compression, add a button such as 'Wait 10 min (sheath sutured), then recheck' that calls act((x) => x.wait(600, "Waiting for the ACT to fall")). Optionally, make chooseClosure('wait-then-compress') spend a first wait interval as well. Add a test that drives the same path: choose wait-then-compress, call wait until a measured ACT is below 180, then startCompression and check femoral-act is correct.

findings.where: src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts decideCompressionAct (say 'The ACT is about N s...') and scoreClosureChoice (say on an 'acceptable' verdict)
findings.problem: The ACT is shown live without being measured. decideCompressionAct speaks the engine's true ACT as a 'safety' line, which say() allows in every mode except exam, so it appears even when no ACT was measured. The 'acceptable' caution ('A device at an ACT above 300 s is discouraged') likewise reveals that the true ACT is above 300 s. The rules forbid showing this outside the guided aids.
findings.fix: Speak only what the operator knows. If no ACT was measured: 'No ACT has been measured since the heparin.' Otherwise: 'The last ACT measured was X s; a femoral sheath comes out by hand once it is below ...'. Base the 300 s caution on the last measured ACT, and send it only when policy.overlays.labels is true; otherwise leave it to the ledger and the debrief.

findings.where: src/ui/access/AccessFluoroView.tsx (outside this package) for closure-fem-branch and closure-fem-old-plug
findings.problem: The femoral angiogram draws the sheath along the common femoral artery when relocateTeamPuncture puts the entry in the accessory profunda, and it draws no filling defect for an old plug. In closure-fem-branch a learner who reads the image correctly would answer 'device OK', and the session marks that wrong. The design's 'small accessory profunda' and 'old plug defect' angiogram presets are therefore missing from the image. The builder flagged this in outOfScope.
findings.fix: The owner of AccessFluoroView.tsx and route.ts femoralSheathPolyline / femoralAngioGeometry should route the sheath along pm.st.arteriotomy.vessel when it is a branch, and draw a filling defect when closureContext.oldPlugDays is set. Until then, mark closure-fem-branch as known-limited, or leave it out of the practice index.

findings.problem: It writes the engine's single vasodilation value (engine.setVasodilation sets it outright; it does not add). The full case's hypotension module also writes that value from its cause runs (hypotensionCauses vasodilationRun). With both active, the last writer wins. When the BP-lowering or the protamine reaction ends, the session sets 0 and wipes out any cause still running.
findings.fix: Run the antihypertensive and the protamine reaction as hypotension-cause runs through the hypotension module when it is attached. Otherwise, keep the session's share separate and send max(session share, the cause's current value). At least never send 0 unless the session's own last value was the one in force.

findings.problem: The closure choice can be clicked again and again, and each click overwrites the femoral-closure-choice decision. A wrong choice followed by the right one leaves no record of the error. answerClosureQuestions, by contrast, scores only the first answer. The choice is also graded against the true ACT, not the last measured ACT the learner decided on.
findings.fix: Score only the first choice. The one legitimate change of plan, wait-then-compress followed by manual compression once the ACT has fallen, can be recorded as a separate item. Grade the ACT rules against the last measured ACT when there is one (keep the true ACT for the outcome model). In ClosurePanel, disable the other choices once one is recorded.

findings.problem: Averaging the position error over the whole compression hides time spent badly placed. In the browser, 4 min on the skin nick (about 15 mm off) followed by 12 min over the hole was recorded as 'Over the arteriotomy (fingers on average 3.7 mm from it)'.
findings.fix: Add offTargetS to CompressionState: seconds pressed with positionError above 5 mm. Set over = offTargetS/pressedS below a labelled MODEL PARAMETER share, and add the minutes off target to the 'given' text.

findings.problem: Some assertions do not depend on the package's events. access-femoral-sheath-act's 'when' is {phase: closure, route: femoral} with no event, so it appears with or without act-high, and the act-high check proves nothing about the tip. The PCI-context check (ids({lab:'pci', events:['bleeding']})) tests tip content only; nothing in the lab raises it. The bradycardia criterion is met only by the test calling scriptVagal itself. The paths that clear act-high (a lower reading, the pull, onSiteClosed) are untested.
findings.fix: Add tests that act-high clears after a measured ACT below 180 s and on startCompression or a sutured sheath. State in the test that the tip is phase-driven, or assert tipScore with act-high is higher than without if the ranking uses events. Leave the PCI line as a content check, but do not cite it as evidence of tip integration.

findings.problem: act-high is held at FEMORAL.actForSheathPullS (180 s) whatever compressionRule is set. Under the Oxford rule chosen in the orders section (below 150-200 s, or 3-4 h after heparin), an ACT of 190 s allows the pull but still raises act-high.
findings.fix: Hold act-high when !actAllowsPull(this.compressionRule, act, sinceLastHeparin) instead of act >= FEMORAL.actForSheathPullS.

findings.problem: Several numbers have no label or source. The slow protamine injection spends a literal 300 s. The swelling diameter Math.sqrt(ml / 0.6) appears in both checkGroin and GroinView. The 'over' cut-off is a literal 6 mm. oldPlugDays <= 90 repeats CLOSURE_ALGORITHM.recentPlugDays. MP_COMPRESSION.raisedSysMmHg (160) grades the BP decision as a clinical threshold. The new MP_COMPRESSION and MP_FEMORAL terms are not in docs/realism/facts (the builder flagged this).
findings.fix: Add protamineSlowS, swellingCmPerSqrtMl and overMm to MP_COMPRESSION and use them in both places. Use CLOSURE_ALGORITHM.recentPlugDays. Word the BP decision's 'expected' as 'a raised pressure (simulator setting)'. Ask the owner of docs/realism/facts to list MP_COMPRESSION and the new MP_FEMORAL terms, and to fix the missing facts/C5.md that closure.ts refers to.

findings.where: src/simulation/session/caseSession.ts slowTick compression step; src/simulation/access/compression.ts stepCompression
findings.problem: While the hands are on, stepCompression returns a new CompressionState (object spread) on every call. The real-time loop calls it about every frame (dt up to 0.1 s), and mapSys() allocates as well. That is avoidable garbage in a per-frame path.
findings.fix: Have stepCompression update the session's state object in place (or a stepCompressionInPlace beside the pure version used by the tests), or step only once the elapsed time since the last step reaches 1 s.

findings.problem: Despite the launch file's comment ('The titles do not give the anatomy or the reaction away'), 'Femoral closure: a calcified groin', 'a groin closed before' and 'more to do later today' name the problem before the angiogram or the chart is read.
findings.fix: Use neutral titles in both files, for example 'Femoral closure: read the entry first (4)' / '(5)' and 'Femoral closure: plan it (2)'. The cue then comes only from the angiogram, the chart history or the attending's plan line. The launch-versus-scenario equality test will keep the two files in step.

findings.problem: Small design-system slips. The finger fills #3A4048, #4A515B and #5B636E are not Clinical Graphite tokens (the others are: base-400/500, ink-soft, danger, accent). The chosen closure button uses seg-btn-active on a .btn. ooze-around-sheath and atheroma have no visible cue anywhere, though no current scenario uses them.
findings.fix: Use token colours, for example base-400, base-600 and ink-faint through currentColor and Tailwind classes, or add named tokens. Mark the chosen closure with a token class such as 'border-accent text-accent' instead of seg-btn-active. If ooze or atheroma is used later, show it as a cue: a 'blood around the sheath' note at the groin, and an irregular lumen on the angiogram.

rejected: Finding 3 (AccessFluoroView/route.ts draw the sheath in the branch and the old-plug filling defect): only partly applied. Those files belong to another package, so the image itself is not changed. I took the reviewer's fallback: closure-fem-branch now has lessonIds [] in both closureFemoral.ts and .launch.ts, so it is out of the practice index (it stays in the picker), with a comment saying why. The old-plug case was left as it is: the chart history gives the cue and the verdict is only 'acceptable'.
Finding 12, last part (cues for ooze-around-sheath and atheroma): not done, because no current scenario uses them. The finding asks for them only if they are used later.

Finding 9, docs part (list MP_COMPRESSION and the new MP_FEMORAL terms in docs/realism/facts, and fix the missing facts/C5.md that closure.ts refers to): outside this package's files. Raised for the owner of docs/realism/facts.

fix.notes:
All 12 findings checked against the code; 11 applied in full or in part, and the parts not done are listed under rejected.

1. Wait (major): ClosurePanel.tsx has a new button 'Wait 10 min (sheath sutured), then recheck'. It calls x.wait(600, ...) and shows while the sheath is in and compression has not started. A new test, src/simulation/session/closureFemoral.test.ts, follows the panel's path on compression-act-high: choose wait-then-compress, wait, measure until a reading is below 180 s, check act-high has cleared, choose compression (recorded as a separate after-wait item), prepare, then startCompression with femoral-act correct.

2. ACT shown without being measured (major): caseSession.ts has new helpers sinceLastHeparinS(), knownAct() (the last reading taken after the last heparin) and decisionEndState(). decideCompressionAct now says either 'No ACT has been measured since the heparin...' or 'The last ACT measured was X s...', never the true ACT. The 'acceptable' caution (an ACT above 300 s) is said only when policy.overlays.labels is on, and is based on the ACT the learner knew.

3. Branch scenario: see rejected.

4. Vasodilation: the session now keeps its own share (vasoOwn). On its first effect it wraps the engine's setVasodilation so the engine always gets the larger of the session's share and the last value from any other writer (vasoOther, read once from snapshot().form.vasodilation). A cause run that stops no longer wipes out the antihypertensive, and the end of the antihypertensive no longer wipes out a running cause. applyVasodilation now runs after the modules' slowTick. A test covers this.

5. Closure choice: only the first choice is scored, and a later click returns that first grade. The one change of plan, wait-then-compress followed by compression, is recorded as 'femoral-closure-after-wait', either from chooseClosure or from startCompression. Choices and answers are graded against the last measured ACT. In the panel the other choices are disabled once one is recorded.

6. Position error: offTargetS added to CompressionState (seconds pressed more than MP_COMPRESSION.overMm = 5 mm off). The summary gains offTargetMin and over (off target for no more than MP_COMPRESSION.offTargetMaxShare = 0.1 of the time). The 'given' text names the minutes off target. compression.test.ts now asserts that 4 minutes on the skin nick is recorded as 'Off the arteriotomy'.

7. Tips test: the closureFemoral.tips.test.ts assertions now state that access-femoral-sheath-act is phase-driven. They assert its 'when' has no act-high and that its tipScore is the same with and without act-high. The PCI check is labelled a content check only. The new test file covers act-high clearing on a lower reading, on startCompression and on keep-suture. No tip in tips.ts keys on act-high, so the event currently has no tip that uses it.

8. act-high is now held when !actAllowsPull(rule, act, sinceLastHeparin). A test shows a reading between 180 and 200 s raises it under Brilakis but not under Oxford.

9. Unlabelled numbers: new MP_COMPRESSION terms protamineSlowS, swellingMlPerCm2 (with an exported swellingCm() used by both checkGroin and GroinView), overMm and offTargetMaxShare. Uses CLOSURE_ALGORITHM.recentPlugDays. The BP decision's expected text now says the systolic threshold is a simulator setting.

10. Per-frame garbage: new stepCompressionInPlace(). The pure stepCompression now wraps it. The session steps the compression in place and reads vitals once, only while hands are on.

11. Titles changed in both files: 'read the entry first (4)', '(5)' and 'Femoral closure: plan it (2)'.

12. Design system: the finger fills now use token classes (fill-base-500, fill-base-400, fill-ink-faint with opacity), the pulse line uses stroke-ink-faint, and the chosen closure is marked with 'border-accent text-accent'.

Existing test changed: compression.test.ts 'Hand compression at ACT 240 s...' now expects a second choice not to overwrite a wrong first one.

Out of scope, for other owners:
(a) AccessFluoroView.tsx and route.ts femoralSheathPolyline / femoralAngioGeometry should draw the sheath along pm.st.arteriotomy.vessel when it is a branch, and an old-plug filling defect when closureContext.oldPlugDays is set. closure-fem-branch's lessonIds can then go back to [PLAN] in both scenario files.
(b) docs/realism/facts should list MP_COMPRESSION (including the new protamineSlowS, swellingMlPerCm2, overMm and offTargetMaxShare) and the new MP_FEMORAL terms, and fix the missing facts/C5.md.
(c) scenarios.test.ts 'decision ledger' fails because of planning.ts 'pre-puncture-checklist', not this package.

checked: Opened a new tab (tab-55) at http://localhost:5173, went to Full procedure and drove it through window.__caseSession plus real clicks, synthetic pointer events and one real mouse drag. Other packages' edits made Vite do a full page reload every 10-20 s, so each check ran as one short script.

Acceptance 'browser: dragging the fingers changes the position error in the debrief': MET. In closure-fem-standard I pressed 'Fingers on, pull the sheath', which starts the hands at the skin nick (0,0), and dragged the GroinView SVG with a real left_click_drag. The hands moved to xMm 17, with the hole at 17.8. Synthetic pointer events gave xMm 18 (centred) or 3 (15 mm caudal). Debrief text for femoral-compression, centred run: 'Over the arteriotomy (fingers on average 0 mm from it)', correct. Caudal for 4 min, then moved over the hole: 'Off the arteriotomy (fingers on average 2.9 mm from it, off it for 4.5 min), enough pressure 76% of the time, 18.6 min', incorrect. In that run the groin check showed 'A swelling in the groin, about 10 cm across' and 'haematoma' was raised.
